name: Diamond In The Rough
descent_text: No route-specific trip report with descent detail could be located for Diamond in the Rough (a 2011 FA by Brandon Workman and Rad Roberts). Because it climbs the same Southwest Face as, and shares an FA partner with, Fire on the Mountain, the best-informed estimate is that parties finish similarly: top out onto the upper mountain, optionally tag the summit via 3rd/4th class scrambling on the upper Corkscrew line, then descend the same 'access ramp' system used off that face — a steep heathered gully down to a granite ledge/ramp, followed by a slabby downclimb that either continues as unprotected low-5th downclimbing or is shortened with one rappel to reach the snowfield below (existing natural anchors on this ramp are reported to be of questionable quality). From snow, traverse clockwise around the peak back to the Southwest Face basin and reverse the approach.

waypoints.name: Bedal Creek/Sloan Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of FR-4096, ~3 mi off the Mountain Loop Highway south of Bedal Campground.
waypoints.directions: Take the Mountain Loop Highway to FR 4096, about 18.25 miles south of Darrington and roughly a mile south of Bedal Campground. The spur is rough and narrow and runs about 3 miles to its end at the Bedal Creek Trailhead, around 2,790 ft, so bring high clearance or 4WD. Bedal Creek Trail #705 starts from the road end. This is the preferred trailhead for this side of Sloan because it avoids the river fords; the Cougar Creek / North Fork Sauk alternative off FR 49 reaches the same basin from the north but makes you ford the North Fork Sauk.

waypoints.name: Climber's trail junction (leaves Bedal Creek trail for the basin)
waypoints.directions: Hike Bedal Creek Trail #705 through old growth and along the creek's steep banks until the maintained tread ends at a large washout, roughly 1.5-2.5 miles in. Scramble the washout — loose boulders and blowdown — to a cairned exit where the climbers' path leaves left under pink flagging at about 3,500 ft.

waypoints.name: Sloan Peak Summit
waypoints.note: Shared summit for Sloan Peak's technical routes.
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' path in steep switchbacks up through the forest band to about 4,900 ft, then talus and meadow to the 5,300 ft Bedal-Sloan saddle, the last reliable water before the wall. From the saddle cross the low connecting ridge into the Southwest Face basin and gain the base of the wall from meadow and talus rather than continuing onto the glacier — glacier ice means you are on the Corkscrew approach, not this one — then climb the nine pitches to the heather ledge where technical climbing ends and scramble 3rd-class terrain to the summit.
